sections.title: Introduction: The Attention Revolution
sections.body:
```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
import math
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

print("="*80)
print("SELF-ATTENTION: THE TRANSFORMER FOUNDATION")
print("="*80)

print("""
🔥 THE PROBLEM WITH RNNs:

Sequential Processing:
   x₁ → RNN → h₁ → RNN → h₂ → RNN → h₃ → ...
   
   ❌ Must process sequentially (can't parallelize!)
   ❌ Long sequences = slow
   ❌ Still struggle with very long dependencies
   ❌ Information bottleneck

🚀 THE SOLUTION: Self-Attention (2017)

"Attention is All You Need" - Vaswani et al.

Key Idea: Every position can attend to EVERY other position
   • Parallel processing! ✅
   • Direct connections between all positions ✅
   • No sequential bottleneck ✅
   • Fast & effective ✅

Self-Attention Question:
   "For each word, which OTHER words should I pay attention to?"

Example: "The cat sat on the mat"
   Processing "sat":
   → High attention to: "cat" (who sat?)
   → Medium attention to: "on" (where?)
   → Lower attention to: "the", "mat"
""")
```

diagrams.title: Scaled dot-product attention
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  x["token embeddings"] --> q["Q = X·Wq"]
  x --> k["K = X·Wk"]
  x --> v["V = X·Wv"]
  q --> s["scores = Q·Kᵀ / √d_k"]
  k --> s
  s --> sm["softmax → attention weights per token"]
  sm --> o["output = weights · V"]
  v --> o
diagrams.explain: Each token builds a query, compares it with every token's key, turns the similarities into weights with softmax and takes the weighted sum of their values. Dividing by √d_k keeps the softmax from saturating. Multi-head attention runs several of these in parallel so different heads can track different relationships.

sections.title: 2. Self-Attention Mathematics
sections.body:
```python
print("\n" + "="*80)
print("SELF-ATTENTION: THE MATH")
print("="*80)

print("""
The Three Matrices: Query, Key, Value (Q, K, V)

Intuition:
   • Query (Q): "What am I looking for?"
   • Key (K):   "What do I contain?"
   • Value (V): "What information do I actually have?"

Think of it like a database:
   • Query = your search terms
   • Key = index/tags on each record
   • Value = actual data in records

For each word:
   Q = W_Q · x  (project input to query space)
   K = W_K · x  (project input to key space)
   V = W_V · x  (project input to value space)

Attention Formula:
   
   Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / √d_k) · V

Step by Step:
   1. QK^T: Compute similarity between all pairs (dot product)
   2. / √d_k: Scale (prevents softmax saturation)
   3. softmax: Convert to probabilities (attention weights)
   4. · V: Weighted sum of values

Matrix Dimensions:
   Input X:  (batch, seq_len, d_model)
   Q, K, V:  (batch, seq_len, d_k)
   QK^T:     (batch, seq_len, seq_len) ← attention matrix!
   Output:   (batch, seq_len, d_k)
""")

class SelfAttention(nn.Module):
    """
    Self-Attention implementation from scratch.
    
    Args:
        d_model: Dimension of input embeddings
        d_k: Dimension of queries and keys
        d_v: Dimension of values
    """
    
    def __init__(self, d_model, d_k, d_v):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.d_k = d_k
        
        # Linear transformations
        self.W_q = nn.Linear(d_model, d_k, bias=False)
        self.W_k = nn.Linear(d_model, d_k, bias=False)
        self.W_v = nn.Linear(d_model, d_v, bias=False)
    
    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        """
        Args:
            x: (batch, seq_len, d_model)
            mask: (batch, seq_len, seq_len) - optional
        Returns:
            output: (batch, seq_len, d_v)
            attention_weights: (batch, seq_len, seq_len)
        """
        # 1. Linear projections
        Q = self.W_q(x)  # (batch, seq_len, d_k)
        K = self.W_k(x)  # (batch, seq_len, d_k)
        V = self.W_v(x)  # (batch, seq_len, d_v)
        
        # 2. Compute attention scores
        scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1))  # (batch, seq_len, seq_len)
        
        # 3. Scale
        scores = scores / math.sqrt(self.d_k)
        
        # 4. Apply mask (optional)
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
        
        # 5. Softmax to get attention weights
        attention_weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)  # (batch, seq_len, seq_len)
        
        # 6. Apply attention to values
        output = torch.matmul(attention_weights, V)  # (batch, seq_len, d_v)
        
        return output, attention_weights

# Example usage
batch_size = 2
seq_len = 5
d_model = 512

# Input sequence
x = torch.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_model)

# Self-attention
attention = SelfAttention(d_model=512, d_k=64, d_v=64)
output, weights = attention(x)

print(f"\nSelf-Attention Example:")
print(f"Input shape:            {x.shape}")
print(f"Output shape:           {output.shape}")
print(f"Attention weights:      {weights.shape}")
print(f"\nAttention matrix (first batch):")
print(weights[0].detach().numpy().round(3))
```

sections.title: 3. Why Scaling by √d_k?
sections.body:
```python
print("\n" + "="*80)
print("WHY SCALE BY √d_k?")
print("="*80)

print("""
Problem: Dot products grow with dimension!

Consider Q·K^T where Q, K ∈ ℝ^d_k:
   • Each element ~ N(0, 1)
   • Dot product = sum of d_k multiplications
   • Variance of dot product ≈ d_k

Example with d_k = 64:
   • Dot products can be very large (±8 or more)
   • Softmax saturates: exp(8) ≈ 3000, exp(-8) ≈ 0.0003
   • Gradients become tiny! (vanishing gradient)

Solution: Scale by √d_k
   • Keeps variance ≈ 1
   • Softmax stays in sensitive region
   • Gradients flow properly
""")

# Demonstration
d_k_values = [16, 64, 256, 1024]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))
axes = axes.flatten()

for idx, d_k in enumerate(d_k_values):
    # Random Q and K
    Q = torch.randn(100, d_k)
    K = torch.randn(100, d_k)
    
    # Compute dot products
    scores_unscaled = torch.matmul(Q, K.T).flatten().numpy()
    scores_scaled = (torch.matmul(Q, K.T) / math.sqrt(d_k)).flatten().numpy()
    
    # Plot
    ax = axes[idx]
    ax.hist(scores_unscaled, bins=50, alpha=0.6, label='Unscaled', color='red')
    ax.hist(scores_scaled, bins=50, alpha=0.6, label='Scaled', color='blue')
    ax.axvline(0, color='black', linestyle='--', linewidth=1)
    ax.set_xlabel('Score Value', fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylabel('Frequency', fontsize=10)
    ax.set_title(f'd_k = {d_k}\nUnscaled std: {scores_unscaled.std():.2f}, Scaled std: {scores_scaled.std():.2f}', 
                 fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
    ax.legend()
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('attention_scaling.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✅ Saved: attention_scaling.png")
print("\nNotice: Scaling keeps standard deviation ≈ 1 regardless of d_k!")
plt.close()
```

sections.title: 4. Attention Visualization
sections.body:
```python
print("\n" + "="*80)
print("VISUALIZING ATTENTION PATTERNS")
print("="*80)

def visualize_attention(attention_weights, tokens, title="Attention Heatmap"):
    """
    Visualize attention weights as a heatmap.
    
    Args:
        attention_weights: (seq_len, seq_len) numpy array
        tokens: List of token strings
        title: Plot title
    """
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
    
    # Create heatmap
    im = plt.imshow(attention_weights, cmap='viridis', aspect='auto')
    
    # Set ticks
    plt.xticks(range(len(tokens)), tokens, rotation=45, ha='right')
    plt.yticks(range(len(tokens)), tokens)
    
    # Labels
    plt.xlabel('Key/Value Position', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    plt.ylabel('Query Position', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    plt.title(title, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
    
    # Colorbar
    cbar = plt.colorbar(im, fraction=0.046, pad=0.04)
    cbar.set_label('Attention Weight', rotation=270, labelpad=20)
    
    # Add text annotations
    for i in range(len(tokens)):
        for j in range(len(tokens)):
            text = plt.text(j, i, f'{attention_weights[i, j]:.2f}',
                          ha="center", va="center", color="white", fontsize=8)
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    return plt

# Example: Simple sentence
tokens = ["The", "cat", "sat", "on", "mat"]
seq_len = len(tokens)

# Create synthetic attention pattern
# "sat" should attend to "cat" and "on"
attention_matrix = torch.zeros(seq_len, seq_len)

# Row 0: "The" - mostly self-attention
attention_matrix[0] = torch.tensor([0.7, 0.1, 0.05, 0.1, 0.05])

# Row 1: "cat" - attends to "The" and itself
attention_matrix[1] = torch.tensor([0.3, 0.5, 0.15, 0.03, 0.02])

# Row 2: "sat" - attends to "cat" (subject) and "on" (location)
attention_matrix[2] = torch.tensor([0.05, 0.5, 0.2, 0.2, 0.05])

# Row 3: "on" - attends to "sat" and "mat"
attention_matrix[3] = torch.tensor([0.05, 0.05, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3])

# Row 4: "mat" - attends to "on"
attention_matrix[4] = torch.tensor([0.05, 0.05, 0.1, 0.4, 0.4])

plt = visualize_attention(attention_matrix.numpy(), tokens, 
                         "Self-Attention: 'The cat sat on mat'")
plt.savefig('attention_heatmap.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✅ Saved: attention_heatmap.png")
print("""
Interpretation:
   • Diagonal: Self-attention (every word attends to itself)
   • "sat" (row 2) → high attention to "cat" (subject)
   • "on" (row 3) → high attention to "mat" (prepositional object)
   • Captures syntactic and semantic relationships!
""")
plt.close()
```

sections.title: 5. Masked Self-Attention (Causal)
sections.body:
```python
print("\n" + "="*80)
print("MASKED SELF-ATTENTION (CAUSAL)")
print("="*80)

print("""
Problem: In language generation, can't see future!

Example: "The cat sat on"
   When predicting next word:
   • Can see: "The", "cat", "sat", "on"
   • Can't see: future words (don't exist yet!)

Solution: Causal Mask
   Prevent attention to future positions

Mask Matrix (5 tokens):
   [[1, 0, 0, 0, 0],   ← Token 0 sees only itself
    [1, 1, 0, 0, 0],   ← Token 1 sees 0,1
    [1, 1, 1, 0, 0],   ← Token 2 sees 0,1,2
    [1, 1, 1, 1, 0],   ← Token 3 sees 0,1,2,3
    [1, 1, 1, 1, 1]]   ← Token 4 sees all previous

Implementation: Set masked positions to -∞ before softmax
   → softmax(-∞) = 0
""")

def create_causal_mask(seq_len):
    """
    Create causal mask for autoregressive generation.
    
    Returns:
        mask: (seq_len, seq_len) lower triangular matrix
    """
    mask = torch.tril(torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len))
    return mask

class CausalSelfAttention(nn.Module):
    """Self-attention with causal masking."""
    
    def __init__(self, d_model, d_k):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.d_k = d_k
        self.W_q = nn.Linear(d_model, d_k, bias=False)
        self.W_k = nn.Linear(d_model, d_k, bias=False)
        self.W_v = nn.Linear(d_model, d_k, bias=False)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        batch_size, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        
        # Projections
        Q = self.W_q(x)
        K = self.W_k(x)
        V = self.W_v(x)
        
        # Attention scores
        scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / math.sqrt(self.d_k)
        
        # Causal mask
        mask = create_causal_mask(seq_len).to(x.device)
        scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
        
        # Softmax and output
        attention_weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        output = torch.matmul(attention_weights, V)
        
        return output, attention_weights

# Example
seq_len = 6
causal_attention = CausalSelfAttention(d_model=512, d_k=64)
x = torch.randn(1, seq_len, 512)
output, weights = causal_attention(x)

print(f"\nCausal Self-Attention Example:")
print(f"Input shape:  {x.shape}")
print(f"Output shape: {output.shape}")
print(f"\nCausal Attention Matrix (lower triangular):")
print(weights[0].detach().numpy().round(3))

# Visualize causal mask
mask = create_causal_mask(8)
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 8))
plt.imshow(mask.numpy(), cmap='RdYlGn', aspect='auto')
plt.colorbar(label='Can Attend (1=Yes, 0=No)')
plt.xlabel('Key Position', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.ylabel('Query Position', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.title('Causal Mask (Autoregressive)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
positions = list(range(8))
plt.xticks(positions, positions)
plt.yticks(positions, positions)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('causal_mask.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✅ Saved: causal_mask.png")
plt.close()

print("""
Use Cases:
   ✅ GPT (language generation)
   ✅ Autoregressive models
   ✅ Decoder in seq2seq
   
   ❌ BERT (needs bidirectional context)
   ❌ Encoder (should see full sequence)
""")
```

sections.title: 6. Self-Attention vs RNN
sections.body:
```python
print("SELF-ATTENTION vs RNN COMPARISON")
```

┌────────────────────┬─────────────────┬─────────────────┐
│ Property           │ RNN             │ Self-Attention  │
├────────────────────┼─────────────────┼─────────────────┤
│ Parallelization    │ ❌ Sequential   │ ✅ Fully parallel│
│ Path Length        │ O(n)            │ O(1)            │
│ Long Dependencies  │ ❌ Difficult    │ ✅ Easy          │
│ Computation        │ O(n·d²)         │ O(n²·d)         │
│ Memory             │ O(n·d)          │ O(n²)           │
│ Inductive Bias     │ ✅ Sequential   │ ❌ None          │
├────────────────────┼─────────────────┼─────────────────┤
│ Best For:          │ Small data,     │ Large data,     │
│                    │ long sequences  │ parallelization │
└────────────────────┴─────────────────┴─────────────────┘

**Path Length:**
- RNN: Information from token i to token j
- Must pass through j-i intermediate states
- Gradient vanishing over long paths

- Self-Attention: Direct connection!
- O(1) path length between ANY two positions
- Gradients flow easily

**Computation Complexity:**
- RNN: O(n) sequential operations, each O(d²)
- Total: O(n·d²)

- Self-Attention: n² attention pairs, each O(d)
- Total: O(n²·d)
- Problem for very long sequences!

**Memory:**
- RNN: Store n hidden states of size d

- Self-Attention: Store n×n attention matrix
- Problem: n=1000 → 1M entries!
- Solution: Efficient attention variants

**Inductive Bias:**
- RNN: Built-in sequential bias (good for small data)

- Self-Attention: No assumptions (needs more data)
- But learns better representations with enough data!

```python
# Computational complexity visualization
seq_lengths = np.array([10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000])
d_model = 512

rnn_ops = seq_lengths * d_model**2

plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.plot(seq_lengths, rnn_ops, 'o-', label='RNN: O(n·d²)', linewidth=2, markersize=8)

plt.yscale('log')

plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
rnn_memory = seq_lengths * d_model

plt.plot(seq_lengths, rnn_memory, 'o-', label='RNN: O(n·d)', linewidth=2, markersize=8)
plt.plot(seq_lengths, attention_memory, 's-', label='Self-Attention: O(n²)', linewidth=2, markersize=8)
plt.xlabel('Sequence Length (n)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.ylabel('Memory Units', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.title('Memory Complexity', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
plt.legend(fontsize=11)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.yscale('log')

```

**Key Insight:**
- Short sequences (n < 512): Self-Attention wins
- Very long sequences (n > 4096): RNN or efficient attention
- Most modern NLP: Self-Attention (n ≈ 512-2048)

sections.title: 7. Complete Self-Attention Example
sections.body:
```python
print("\n" + "="*80)
print("COMPLETE SELF-ATTENTION EXAMPLE")
print("="*80)

class ScaledDotProductAttention(nn.Module):
    """
    Scaled Dot-Product Attention.
    
    The fundamental attention mechanism used in Transformers.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, temperature, dropout=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.temperature = temperature
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
    
    def forward(self, q, k, v, mask=None):
        """
        Args:
            q: Queries (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
            k: Keys (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
            v: Values (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_v)
            mask: Optional mask (batch, 1, 1, seq_len) or (batch, 1, seq_len, seq_len)
        
        Returns:
            output: (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_v)
            attention: (batch, n_heads, seq_len, seq_len)
        """
        # 1. Compute attention scores
        scores = torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1))
        scores = scores / self.temperature
        
        # 2. Apply mask if provided
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
        
        # 3. Apply softmax
        attention = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        attention = self.dropout(attention)
        
        # 4. Apply attention to values
        output = torch.matmul(attention, v)
        
        return output, attention

# Example usage
batch_size = 4
seq_len = 10
d_k = 64

q = torch.randn(batch_size, 1, seq_len, d_k)  # 1 head for simplicity
k = torch.randn(batch_size, 1, seq_len, d_k)
v = torch.randn(batch_size, 1, seq_len, d_k)

attention_module = ScaledDotProductAttention(temperature=math.sqrt(d_k))
output, attention_weights = attention_module(q, k, v)

print(f"\nScaled Dot-Product Attention:")
print(f"Query shape:      {q.shape}")
print(f"Key shape:        {k.shape}")
print(f"Value shape:      {v.shape}")
print(f"Output shape:     {output.shape}")
print(f"Attention shape:  {attention_weights.shape}")

# Verify attention weights sum to 1
attention_sums = attention_weights.sum(dim=-1)
print(f"\nAttention weights sum (should be 1.0):")
print(f"Mean: {attention_sums.mean():.6f}")
print(f"Std:  {attention_sums.std():.6f}")

print("""
✅ Self-Attention Summary:

1. Core Idea: Each position attends to all positions

2. Three Projections:
   • Query (Q): What I'm looking for
   • Key (K): What I contain
   • Value (V): What I contribute

3. Attention Formula:
   Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T / √d_k) · V

4. Benefits:
   ✅ Parallel computation
   ✅ Long-range dependencies
   ✅ Direct connections
   ✅ Interpretable

5. Challenges:
   ❌ O(n²) complexity
   ❌ No inductive bias
   ❌ Needs positional encoding

Next: Multi-Head Attention (multiple attention patterns!)
""")
```

sections.title: Summary
sections.body:
### Self-Attention Key Concepts

```
1. Purpose: Every position attends to every other position

2. Components:
   • Query (Q): "What am I looking for?"
   • Key (K): "What do I contain?"
   • Value (V): "What information do I have?"

3. Formula:
   Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T / √d_k) · V

4. Scaling: √d_k prevents softmax saturation

5. Causal Masking: Prevents seeing future (generation tasks)

6. Advantages over RNN:
   ✅ Parallel processing
   ✅ O(1) path length
   ✅ Better long-range dependencies

7. Disadvantages:
   ❌ O(n²) memory and computation
   ❌ No sequential inductive bias
```

### When to Use Self-Attention

```
✅ Good For:
   • Sequences up to ~4K tokens
   • Parallel training
   • Long-range dependencies
   • Large datasets
   • Tasks needing interpretability

❌ Not Ideal For:
   • Very long sequences (>8K)
   • Limited compute/memory
   • Very small datasets
   • Streaming/online processing
```

### PyTorch Quick Reference

```python
# Self-attention from scratch
Q = W_q(x)
K = W_k(x)
V = W_v(x)
scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / math.sqrt(d_k)
attention = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
output = torch.matmul(attention, V)

# With causal mask
mask = torch.tril(torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len))
scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
```
